items.text: President [[p:Isaac Herzog]] gave [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]], leader of the centrist Yashar party, the first mandate to form Israel's next government after 67 of 120 incoming MKs recommended him, a setback for Prime Minister [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]]. Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by two weeks, and says an emergency coalition will need unconventional steps and compromise from all sides.
items.outlet: The Times of Israel; AP (via PBS)
items.notes: Election held 27 Oct. Bloc counts differ: AP gives Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats, Eisenkot's 48, Arab-led parties 19; ToI says 46 MKs back Netanyahu. Formal ceremony evening of 8 Nov. On 9 Nov Trump called the two men's policies very similar (ToI liveblog).

items.text: An explosive-laden drone hit the [[p:Dana Gas]]-operated Khor Mor gas facility in Sulaimani province late on 8 Nov, starting a fire and halting production. The [[p:Kurdistan Regional Government]] says 2,500–2,800 MW was lost, over 70% of the region's power. No one has claimed the attack; Baghdad ordered a joint investigation.
items.notes: No official attribution. Unofficial accounts cited by Kurdistan24 point to a launch near Tuz Khurmatu; claims of an Iranian strike are unsupported. Al Jazeera says any link to the US–Iran war is unclear. Same facility hit in Nov 2025. No casualties. No restart date from Dana Gas.

items.text: The COP31 climate conference opened in Antalya after a delay over whether climate finance would be on the agenda. Türkiye holds the presidency under [[p:Murat Kurum]], while Australia's [[p:Chris Bowen]] leads negotiations under a power-sharing deal. The Trump administration sent no officials, and few breakthroughs are expected amid an oil price shock.
items.notes: Runs 9–20 Nov; World Leaders' Summit 11–12 Nov. Türkiye is pushing a voluntary pledge to raise electricity's share of global energy use to 35% by 2035. TRT World is Turkish state media. Outlook ('few breakthroughs') is AFP's assessment.

items.text: The [[p:Electoral Commission of South Africa]] declared final local election results: the [[p:African National Congress]] came first with 30.76%, its worst result since 1994, ahead of the [[p:Democratic Alliance (South Africa)|Democratic Alliance]] (24.64%), the [[p:uMkhonto weSizwe Party|MK Party]] (9.76%) and the [[p:Economic Freedom Fighters|EFF]] (6.22%). Only 74 of 213 councils have a majority, so coalition talks begin, notably in the Gauteng metros.
items.notes: Borderline Tier 1 (pressure on the GNU partners). Hung-council counts conflict between outlets (127–142). Turnout 52%. ActionSA 5.67%. Ramaphosa urged good-faith coalition talks.

items.text: Kremlin spokesman [[p:Dmitry Peskov]] confirmed Russia will join the US-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov, with presidential aide [[p:Vladimir Medinsky]] {{note: Former Russian culture minister who headed Moscow's delegation at the 2022 and 2025 Istanbul talks with Ukraine.}} heading the delegation. Peskov said a US–Russia–China leaders' meeting around APEC was also being explored.
items.notes: Opinion: analysis. Kremlin confirmation via RIA Novosti/TASS. ISW (3 Nov) assesses Medinsky's appointment signals stalling (analysis). Zelensky said in Berlin on 3 Nov he hopes the format opens the way to a leaders' meeting.

items.text: Kyiv confirmed that [[p:Rustem Umerov]] will lead Ukraine's team in Abu Dhabi, correcting reports that presidential office head [[p:Kyrylo Budanov]] would. Budanov, [[p:Davyd Arakhamia]] and [[p:Serhiy Kyslytsya]] are also on the team; Budanov told CBS not to expect a major breakthrough.
items.notes: Ukraine plans to raise the Komyshuvakha strike. Single-source headline (8 Nov): French FM Barrot said Europeans will be well represented in Abu Dhabi; not read in full. Ukrainian MFA said on 30 Oct Europe would join the process but not the trilateral group.

items.text: Foreign Minister [[p:Andrii Sybiha]] set out Kyiv's Abu Dhabi priorities in Warsaw: security guarantees, Black Sea de-escalation, an energy truce, return of children and prisoner exchanges. On 27 Oct he had said the working-level group was not senior enough for the most sensitive issues.
items.notes: The energy-ceasefire idea is a US proposal Zelensky backed in September.

items.text: The [[p:European Commission]] hosted pre-Abu Dhabi coordination talks with US, Ukrainian, NATO, German, French, British and World Bank officials on reconstruction, security guarantees and Ukraine's 2027 funding gap. Zelensky held a 90-minute call with [[p:Steve Witkoff]] and [[p:Jared Kushner]] the same day.
items.notes: Umerov said work on 'the document' is under way, no details. Zelensky said in Berlin (3 Nov) Ukraine needs an extra €70bn from Europe next year.

items.text: The six-day local ceasefire in occupied Oleshky expired on 1 Nov without extension; neither side reported violations. [[p:Melania Trump]], who mediated, said nearly 800 people were evacuated. A Ukrainian official said Russia rejected Kyiv's proposal to extend it.
items.notes: Pope Leo XIV was also involved. About 2,000 civilians were in Oleshky when the truce began; 167 evacuated on the final day per Ukraine's military. White House ceremony on Oleshky 5 Nov.

items.text: A Kremlin-linked source told journalist Farida Rustamova that [[p:Vladimir Putin]] welcomed the 26 Oct call from Finnish President [[p:Alexander Stubb]] and Norwegian PM [[p:Jonas Gahr Støre]] as a possible start of substantive talks with Europe. Moscow reportedly sees both as less hard-line than Berlin, Paris or London.
items.notes: Original vlast.is post could not be opened; via Meduza's English summary. Single anonymous source. Kyiv says the call was coordinated with it. FT said Putin spent much of the call on medieval history; Støre denied this.

items.text: The [[p:Institute for the Study of War]] estimates Russian forces had a net loss of about 27 km² in October, a second straight monthly loss, gaining only in Sumy and Zaporizhzhia oblasts. ISW assesses Moscow has largely dropped offensives on the Kupiansk and Borova axes; Dobropillia remains its main effort.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Opinion: analysis. Including infiltration zones ISW puts the net loss at 76 km². Ukraine's General Staff claims 54,400 Russian casualties in October, its highest monthly figure (Ukrainian estimate).

items.text: ISW assesses from geolocated footage that Russian troops have likely consolidated positions in north-western Kostiantynivka. Ukraine's General Staff reported 201 clashes on 3 Nov, 24 on the Kostiantynivka axis.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Russian milbloggers claim a strike on a Kazennyi Torets bridge in Kramatorsk. Ukrainian counterattacks reported near Dobropillia, Orikhiv and Lyman.

items.text: Military observer Kostyantyn Mashovets says Ukrainian forces cleared most of Mala Tokmachka, south-east of Orikhiv, while Russian troops infiltrate west of Orikhiv via the drained Kakhovka reservoir bed. ISW recorded no confirmed Russian advances on the Huliaipole or Dobropillia axes.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Mashovets' account unverified. A Russian milblogger claimed advances near Novohryshyne; ISW did not confirm.

items.text: Zelensky said Ukraine's front-line positions are the strongest in a long time, citing claimed recaptures of over 800 km² by air assault forces and over 200 km² by Operation Vivaldi in Donetsk oblast.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Ukrainian claims; time frame unclear. Ukraine's MoD reportedly asked five European states for 10% of their interceptor stocks.

items.text: Russia's largest attack on Ukraine's energy system this year hit nine oblasts with, by Zelensky's count, 289 drones, 17 ballistic and 59 cruise missiles. [[p:Ukrenergo]] reported over 20 hits and emergency outages, and Kyiv's water supply was cut citywide for over a day, the worst outage of the full-scale war.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: ISW citing Air Force data: ~18% of ballistic and 83% of cruise missiles intercepted. Russian MoD claimed hits on four power plants and two substations. A strike on a Kharkiv hospital injured 73.

items.text: The death toll from Russia's 2 Nov aerial-bomb strike on an aid point in Komyshuvakha rose to 55, Zaporizhzhia's governor said. Latvia, holding the [[p:United Nations Security Council]] presidency, requested an emergency council meeting.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Tolls vary by date (53 on 6 Nov per Kyiv Post/KI URL; 55 per governor on 7 Nov). Russian milbloggers claim the building housed a drone post (unverified). No UNSC meeting date found.

items.text: A Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at Dnipro's main railway station, killing at least 14, according to [[p:Ukrzaliznytsia]] and regional officials. Russian attacks killed at least 19 nationwide that day.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Multi-agency wire report; no separate cross-check opened.

items.text: Russian officials reported a mass Ukrainian drone raid toward Moscow: [[p:TASS]] said 613 drones were launched and Mayor [[p:Sergey Sobyanin]] said 231 were downed near the city; the defence ministry claimed 1,214 intercepted nationwide.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: All figures Russian, unverified. Came as Moscow hosted a summit with African leaders.

items.text: [[p:Lukoil]]'s NORSI refinery in Kstovo, Russia's fourth-largest, was reportedly hit by drones; ISW also reported strikes on a Rostov chemical plant and Su-34s at Marinovka airfield.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Source: Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channels; no official claim. Su-34 losses are a Ukrainian claim. Al Jazeera (6 Nov): eight Russian refineries hit in seven days.

items.text: A drone attack set fire to the Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl, one of Russia's five largest; the governor acknowledged damage and said 124 drones were engaged.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: By 5 Nov ISW also reported strikes on the Ryazan refinery and an Oryol plant.

items.text: The Afipsky refinery in Krasnodar Krai was reportedly hit by drones; regional authorities confirmed a fire at an unnamed Afipsk enterprise, blaming debris.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Ukraine has not commented. Seventh attack on the plant in 2026 per UNITED24.

items.text: The [[p:Verkhovna Rada]] voted to extend martial law (293 votes) and general mobilisation (281) for 90 days, to 29 Jan 2027.
items.notes: Bills 16182 and 16183.

items.text: In 'Operation Carthage' the [[p:National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine|NABU]] and anti-corruption prosecutors say they exposed a group that paid officials in the [[p:Security Service of Ukraine|SBU]], police and prosecution to protect scam call centres, drug sales and counterfeiting. The acting SBU head dismissed two senior officials; suspicion notices followed on 5 Nov.
items.notes: Censor.NET sources name an SBU major general (Serhii Duka); NABU has not confirmed names. Reported searches linked to Klymenko denied by the NSDC. Ex-Prosecutor General Kravchenko calls the case political revenge.

items.text: The US State Department approved a possible $2.1bn sale of 500 PAC-3 MSE Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, financed by Canada, Germany and Norway. Zelensky warned deliveries could take years and asked allies for interceptors from stock this winter.
items.notes: Approval of a possible sale, no delivery timeline. NATO commander Grynkewich said PURL deliveries were not delayed.

items.text: The EU disbursed €4.36bn to Ukraine under the Ukraine Support Loan: €3.7bn of macro-financial aid and €660m for defence.
items.notes: Conditional on bills passed in mid-October. No new decision found on the reparations loan.

items.text: [[p:Novaya Gazeta]] {{note: Independent Moscow newspaper founded in 1993 by journalists from Komsomolskaya Pravda, with Mikhail Gorbachev's backing; editor Dmitry Muratov shared the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize.}} announced it is shutting down, closing its Moscow office on 9 Nov. It said authorities had blocked its sites, seized its printing house, revoked its registration and cut off donations, blaming the [[p:Federal Security Service|FSB]], Justice Ministry and prosecutors.
items.notes: Whole editorial staff designated foreign agents in Sept 2026; executive editor Oleg Roldugin awaits trial (Meduza). No Kremlin comment.

items.text: The [[p:State Duma]] passed the 2027–29 budget in first reading: 'national defence' spending rises about 32% to 17.1 trillion roubles in 2027 while health, housing and social spending are cut. It adds a windfall tax on cement, fertiliser and gold producers and a 22% tax on passive income.
items.notes: Translated from Russian. Vote 372 for, 51 abstentions. 2027 deficit planned at 5.4 trillion roubles; 2026 deficit put at 7.3 trillion, about double plan. Second reading 19 Nov.

items.text: Two tankers that left Primorsk listing the US East Coast as destination turned toward Brazil and the Mediterranean, per Kpler and MarineTraffic data, casting doubt on the US–Russia diesel arrangement. Envoy [[p:Kirill Dmitriev]] called the report fake; New Jersey Governor [[p:Mikie Sherrill]] told ports to turn the cargoes away.
items.notes: Tankers Talisman and Leruo; a third now 'for orders'. OFAC exemption runs to 7 Apr. Deal terms undisclosed.

items.text: Reuters reports a group led by US billionaire [[p:Todd Boehly]] is close to acquiring [[p:Lukoil]]'s foreign assets by swapping frozen Lukoil shares bought cheaply from Western funds. Any deal needs [[p:Office of Foreign Assets Control|OFAC]] approval; its negotiation licence runs to 21 Nov.
items.notes: Reuters original not opened. Other reported backers: IHC, Al Hail, US DFC. Carlyle withdrew last month.

items.text: [[p:Vladimir Putin]] decreed temporary state management of [[p:Japan Tobacco]]'s Russian subsidiaries, and Tokyo protested. Zerkalo, citing United24, says control went to a firm co-founded by a former intelligence officer.
items.notes: Ownership details unverified. Business valued at roughly $3.1–3.7bn by analysts.

items.text: Belarusian hacker group Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow claim to have stolen about 23TB from Russia's statistics agency Rosstat, including records of war deaths. Rosstat confirmed an attack but says no data leaked.
items.notes: Casualty figures conflict: TechRadar cites ~1.58m dead posted by hackers; Zerkalo cites 393,881 (Cyber Partisans) and 450,100 (Silent Crow). Unverified.

items.text: Moscow police rounded up an estimated 150–300 young people in Kitai-Gorod in what the [[p:Ministry of Internal Affairs (Russia)|Interior Ministry]] called a preventive measure; detainees reported beatings and some were handed military summonses.
items.notes: Two summonses specifically documented. Translated from Russian.

items.text: Russia's Justice Ministry listed two unregistered anti-war parties as 'foreign agents': Mirnaya Rossiya, founded by [[p:Ilya Yashin]], and Rassvet, founded by Yekaterina Duntsova.

The FSB opened a treason case against Gennady Stepakhno, 76, a former Murmansk regional deputy speaker from the [[p:Communist Party of the Russian Federation|Communist Party]], accusing him of passing documents to Ukrainian intelligence.
items.notes: Detained 9 Oct; case public 29 Oct.

items.text: Finance Ministry data show October oil and gas revenue up 9.3% year on year to about 971bn roubles on higher Urals prices; January–October revenue is still 14% lower than a year earlier.
items.outlet: Reuters via The Moscow Times (Russian service)
items.notes: Translated from Russian. Urals averaged $92.08 in September.

items.text: [[p:Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe|OSCE]] Secretary-General [[p:Feridun Sinirlioğlu]] met [[p:Alexander Lukashenko]] in Minsk, the first OSCE chief's visit since 2019. [[p:Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]] called it an unearned reward; [[p:Viasna Human Rights Centre|Viasna]] counts 887 political prisoners.
items.notes: Lavrov attended the same Minsk security conference. Lukashenko's claim there that the war would end within months is rhetoric, not logged.

items.text: The Kyiv Independent reports that US envoy John Coale's push to reopen Lithuanian ports to Belarusian potash is largely his own initiative with little backing in Washington; Lithuania has no plans to shift.
items.reporter: Jimmy Rushton; Tim Zadorozhnyy; Martin Fornusek
items.notes: Anonymous US and European officials; Coale did not respond.

items.text: [[p:Alexander Lukashenko]] told the Interior Ministry to draft a new amnesty bill aimed mainly at women; scope and timing were not announced.
items.notes: Translated from Russian. 2025 amnesty excluded 'extremist' convictions, i.e. most political prisoners.

items.text: Reuters reports, citing four sources, that Pentagon officials including policy chief [[p:Elbridge Colby]] privately urged the Baltic states to tone down public warnings about Russia. Estonia's defence ministry says no such message reached it officially.
items.notes: Anonymous sources; Pentagon declined to discuss private talks; no Lithuanian or Latvian reaction found.

items.text: President [[p:Nicușor Dan]] received Colby in Bucharest, and Romania reportedly offered to share the cost of keeping US troops there. Colby gave no commitment and said [[p:Donald Trump]] is expected to decide US force levels in Europe in early December.
items.notes: Cost-sharing offer from unnamed presidency sources. Dan's description of the Black Sea as among the most dangerous maritime regions is translated from Romanian. About 1,000 US troops remain in Romania.

items.text: Munich prosecutors said two Belarusian men held since 7 Oct are suspected of planning a paid arson attack near Nuremberg for a foreign state. Romania is seeking their extradition, with a Ukrainian held in Poland, over the 14 Sept arson at a Brașov arms-maker site.
items.notes: Prosecutors did not name the state; Der Spiegel reports they worked for Russia. Moscow denies sabotage.

items.text: Lithuanian police named two German dual nationals in their twenties as terrorism suspects in the 18 Oct attempted arson of a Vilnius firm storing [[p:Starlink]] gear; both are in custody in Germany on Bulgarian warrants and are linked to similar cases in Poland and Bulgaria.
items.notes: Russia link drawn by Lithuanian politicians, not police.

items.text: Poland sent extra police, including counter-terrorism units, to the Kaliningrad border after sabotage warnings that PM [[p:Donald Tusk]] says came from US and Polish military intelligence. Tusk says a possible provocation near Sępopol was thwarted on 3 Nov; no one crossed.
items.notes: Per Tusk, the warning came from US EUCOM chief Gen. Grynkewich; no direct NATO statement. Separate 7 Nov Kraków shooting (six dead) not logged: single secondary source, officials see no Russia link.

items.text: Poland's Internal Security Agency arrested six people suspected of spying for Russia and smuggling ammunition components worth over 2m zloty to Kaliningrad.
items.notes: Four charged with espionage.

items.text: Latvia fired an interceptor drone on 1 Nov at an intruding drone, likely a Russian Geran type, that returned to Russia; another drone resembling Ukrainian models triggered an alert on 3 Nov and may have crashed in Balvi district.
items.notes: Drone types and origins unconfirmed.

items.text: Suspected cyberattacks hit supermarket freezer systems in five EU countries including Estonia, after similar October attacks in France and the Netherlands; no one has claimed responsibility.
items.notes: No government attribution to Russia; thread deliberately left blank.

items.text: Estonia's internal security service expelled Russian citizen Leonid Karabeshkin, a former academic and ERR Russian-language reporter, saying he had links to Russian intelligence.
items.notes: Security service claims, untested in court.

items.text: A new US Army rotational unit has arrived in Estonia for nine months, ending a gap since the summer.
items.notes: Apache Troop, 5-4 Cavalry. Confirmed by US Embassy.

items.text: The [[p:European Commission]] turned down a Baltic request for an extra €500m for an anti-drone system; Commissioner [[p:Andrius Kubilius]] pointed to SAFE loans instead.
items.notes: About €21bn left in SAFE; new call soon.

items.text: Moldova said Transnistrian leader [[p:Vadim Krasnoselsky]] faces a five-year ban on leaving Moldova after [[p:Vladimir Putin]] gave him a state award in Moscow on 4 Nov, which Chișinău called a provocation timed with talks on the region's winter gas.
items.notes: Quotes in NewsMaker translated from Romanian; one analyst called it 'dust in the eyes' (translation) and questioned the legal basis. Not confirmed whether he has returned.

items.text: President [[p:Maia Sandu]] opened the 400 kV Vulcănești–Chișinău line to Romania, cutting reliance on the Russian-owned Cuciurgan plant in Transnistria, and said Moldova now buys no Russian gas.
items.notes: 'Zero Russian gas' is Sandu's claim. Gas-shortage emergency runs to 20 Nov.

items.text: Moldova's defence ministry said two aerostat-type objects crossed its airspace over Drochia and Soroca, one from the direction of Ukraine's Vinnytsia region.
items.notes: Operator and purpose unknown.
